claim: Cáceres tapas/gastrobar spots include Maná Chef Alia (Plaza Santa Clara), Nolasco and Borona Bistró in the centre, Torre de Sande in the old town for Iberian sausages and local cheeses, and Restaurante Miga on Plaza Mayor serving Extremaduran migas.
quote: Restaurante Miga (Plaza Mayor) Features the "famous Extremaduran migas" alongside modern interpretations of traditional recipes. Torre de Sande (Old Town) Specializes in regional offerings including Iberian sausages, local cheeses, and grilled meats with charming terrace seating.

claim: Migas extremeñas are a shepherd's dish of day-old bread crumbled and slow-fried with olive oil, garlic, panceta, often chorizo and pimentón, served widely in Cáceres bars on and around Plaza Mayor and as a breakfast in cafeterias.
quote: The essential ingredients include: Day-old chopped bread... Panceta (bacon), Olive oil, Garlic. Common additions are chorizo, red and green peppers, and pimentón (paprika)... in the bars of the Plaza, as well as in those that surround it.

claim: Cáceres's flagship local products are jamón ibérico de bellota, extra virgin olive oil, pimentón de la Vera (sweet, bittersweet and spicy, smoke-dried over oak), Torta del Casar cheese, and Iberian cured meats like bellota chorizo, salchichón, lomo and morcilla.
quote: Cáceres is known for jamón ibérico de bellota, extra virgin olive oil, pimentón de La Vera, and torta del Casar... It comes in three varieties—sweet, bittersweet, and spicy.

claim: Torta del Casar is a DOP raw-milk sheep cheese from Casar de Cáceres, made with thistle-flower (vegetable) rennet, prized for its creamy, spoonable paste with bitter-salty notes; PDO since 1996 and a World Cheese Awards 2019 Super Gold winner.
quote: made using traditional methods from the raw milk of Merino and Entrefina sheep and thistle flower extract... awarded "Super Gold" at the World Cheese Awards 2019.

claim: Jamón ibérico de bellota DOP Dehesa de Extremadura comes from Iberian pigs fattened only on acorns during the montanera, requires 3–6 hectares of wooded dehesa per animal, cures a minimum of 36 months (often 48+), and has been an EU PDO since 1996.
quote: The European Union recognized Dehesa de Extremadura as a Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) in 1996... fed exclusively on acorns and natural pastures of the dehesa during the montanera... The minimum curing time is 36 months, but can exceed 48 months.

claim: The Ribera del Guadiana Wine and Cava Route runs 'The Colors of the Harvest', a Cáceres Provincial Council-backed programme of winery visits and wine-and-cheese events across towns like Casar de Cáceres, Trujillo, Guadalupe and Cañamero.
quote: The Colors of the Harvest is an initiative by the Ribiera del Guadiana Wine and Cava Route, with the support of the Cáceres Provincial Council... such charming towns as Romangordo, Casar de Cáceres, Trujillo, Guadalupe, Cañamero, and Acehúche.

claim: Ribera del Guadiana is Extremadura's only DO wine region, spanning Cáceres and Badajoz provinces with roughly 26 wineries and around 33,200 hectares of vines, offering a wine route of cellar visits and tastings paired with regional products.
quote: Ribiera del Guadiana is a wine-producing region located in the province of Cáceres and Badajoz... the only wine-producing area in Extremadura... with 26 wineries, its vines stretch 33200 hectares.

claim: Casar de Cáceres-based shops such as La Despensa del Casar and Cáceres delis like Ibéricos Alvarado and El Siglo (C/ Moret 1) sell Torta del Casar, jamón ibérico and embutidos to take home, in-store or online.
quote: La Despensa del Casar - offers a large selection of Extremaduran products including cheeses, jamón ibérico, and embutidos.

claim: Cáceres tapas crawls cluster around the Roman Theatre (e.g. Vía de la Tapa) and the monumental quarter, with spots like Restaurant Tuétano showcasing DO Ribera del Guadiana wines; star products include Torta del Casar, patatera and Morcilla de Guadalupe.
quote: tapas next to the Roman Theater at Vía de La Tapa restaurant, or enjoying D.O. Rivera del Guadiana wines at Restaurant Tuétano... star products including its soft paste cheeses D.O. Torta del Casar, patatera, and Morcilla de Guadalupe.
